description: This file defines a QuestionGeneratorAgent class which uses a state machine (LangGraph) to orchestrate the process of generating questions for a medical exam preparation app. It includes methods to generate single questions asynchronously, manage question generation workflows, and batch process multiple questions with concurrency. It references custom node classes, configuration settings, and external graph components.

classes.name: QuestionState
classes.description: TypedDict schema defining the state object used during question generation workflow, including fields for context, validation, question draft, and error info.

classes.name: QuestionGeneratorAgent
classes.description: An agent class that manages question generation using a state machine workflow, with methods for generating single or multiple questions asynchronously, handling validation, retries, and batching.

methods.name: __init__(self)
methods.description: Initializes the agent, setting up nodes and building the question generation workflow graph.

methods.name: StateGraph _build_graph(self)
methods.description: Constructs the LangGraph workflow with nodes, edges, and conditional routing for question validation and regeneration.

methods.name: str _should_regenerate(self, state: QuestionState)
methods.description: Decides whether to regenerate a question based on validation results, confidence, and attempts, with logging.

methods.name: Optional[Dict[str,Any]] generate_single_question( self, chapter_id: int, difficulty: str = "intermediate", include_images: bool = False )
methods.description: Asynchronously generates and returns a single question for a specified chapter, difficulty, and options, handling errors.

methods.name: List[Dict[str,Any]] generate_batch_questions( self, chapter_id: int, count: int, difficulty: str = "intermediate", include_images: bool = False, max_concurrent: int = 3 )
methods.description: Generates multiple questions concurrently in batches, respecting maximum concurrency, and returns a list of questions.
